scope: Installed Windows 11 10.0.29683 on ARM64; x64/x86/x86-LAA are execution views on that kernel, not independent kernels.
material-observations: Optional SIZE_T publication is late, and may alias source or destination; WoW64 pre-reads a ULONG slot and suppresses publication after a failed read.
Source PAGE_GUARD is retained; a reached destination guard is consumed. Execute-only source pages can be read by the service.
A zero length ignores invalid/wrong-type/insufficient-access handles but still applies native extent and optional count checks.
A partial count can exceed bytes actually written: an 8-byte store across a boundary with four writable bytes returns PARTIAL_COPY/count4 without any destination byte change.
Large faulting copies publish completed fourteen-page blocks. Fully readable/writable overlapping copies expose a 65536-byte snapshot boundary.
Working-set captures retain the host's residency/prefetch observations. Exact host prefetch breadth is not a guest paging contract and is not normalized into byte/protection/status evidence.

assumptions.assumption: Current-process reads use actual guest mappings and existing process grants; no guest request selects host memory.
assumptions.stress-test: foreign process with valid read grant and armed count guard
assumptions.falsification-probe: foreign service completes or consumes the guard

assumptions.assumption: Native copy stores and count/probe ordering must be derived from original NTDLL captures for each selected execution view.
assumptions.stress-test: all 11024 immutable calls plus native replay repeat
assumptions.falsification-probe: any status, destination byte or protection mismatch

bounded-scope.item: Foreign-process virtual address-space ownership is not yet modeled by this group.
bounded-scope.behavior: Explicit unsupported frontier before caller mutation; never host forwarding.

bounded-scope.item: The native corpus uses one ARM64 kernel build; independent x64 kernel behavior remains a distinct validation surface.
bounded-scope.falsification-probe: Run the native producer on an independent x64 kernel and replay all results without weakened assertions.
